saints.name: Sts. John and Paul
saints.title: Martyrs
saints.shortBlurb: Two brothers of Rome, martyred under Julian the Apostate, whose names are spoken in the Canon of the Mass…
biography: Their ancient acts, much embroidered though they are, tell that John and Paul were brothers and officers in the household of Constantia, a daughter of Constantine, who had withdrawn to their house on the Caelian Hill to serve God and the poor. When Julian the Apostate pressed them to return to court and sacrifice, he gave them ten days to decide; they spent them giving their goods to the needy.

On 26 June, about the year 362, they were beheaded secretly within their own house by the officer Terentianus, and it was put about that they had merely been sent into exile. Three who had ministered to them, Crispus, Crispinianus, and Benedicta, shared their fate and were buried near them.

Their tomb was venerated from the fifth century; the senator Byzantius and his son Pammachius made the house a church, today's Basilica of Santi Giovanni e Paolo, beneath which the frescoed Roman rooms came to light in the nineteenth century. Their names stand in the Roman Canon of the Mass, invoked among the martyrs to this day.
saints.knownFor: Their martyrdom under Julian; named in the Roman Canon.

sources.text: The Roman Martyrology (1914 English ed.; public domain)
